Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `main` @ `08c4132ec756bf6acc2c12a1602a19d441de0ff2` (no integration branch metadata, so no mismatch).

## Implementation plan: stop CI event labels from changing the security-audit contract test's engine (PR #6780 CI failure)

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends _run_security_audit
Scope-mode justification: The failure comes from the test harness, not from production code. The fix is one default added to the env block the existing `_run_security_audit` helper already builds, plus one regression test. The regression test reproduces the CI condition: an `ai:engine-claude` label in the job's event payload. That costs well under 30 lines and adds no new dependency or interface, so the complete option is in scope (Boil the Lake). §6 order is Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed: a test that passes or fails depending on the PR's labels is a correctness problem. Production engine selection (`scripts/claude_engine.py`, `scripts/ai_engine.sh`, `scripts/security_audit.sh`) stays unchanged.

### Root cause (confirmed from code, not only from the triage hypothesis)
- `tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py::_run_security_audit` (line ~246) copies `os.environ`. Line ~250 then drops every key starting with `AI_ENGINE` or `CLAUDE_`, so `AI_ENGINE_LABELS` is never set unless a test passes it through `extra_env`.
- `scripts/claude_engine.py::work_item_labels` (lines ~330-355) reads `AI_ENGINE_LABELS` only when the key is present. Otherwise it reads the labels of `issue` / `pull_request` from `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`. That variable is not stripped, so in CI it points at the real PR event payload.
- `resolve` (lines ~394-414) checks labels (`ai:codex`, then `ai:engine-claude`) before `AI_ENGINE_SECURITY_AUDIT`. PR #6780 (`ai/issue-6776`) can carry `ai:engine-claude` (implement copies the engine label onto the PR; see `AI_ENGINE_PR_LABEL`). In that case the first case of `test_security_audit_codex_engine_or_codex_label_never_starts_claude` (line 2722, `{"AI_ENGINE_SECURITY_AUDIT": "codex"}`) resolves to Claude, and the assertion `"security-audit: engine=codex" in proc.stdout` fails.
- The same leak can also break `test_security_audit_role_default_runs_claude` (it asserts `source=default`) and any other `_claude_engine_audit` caller.
- Other harnesses already guard against this. `tests/test_claude_engine.py:38-39` has the comment "CI jobs carry a real GITHUB_EVENT_PATH whose labels would leak in" and strips it. `tests/test_ai_engine.py:130` does the same. This harness never had that guard.

Conflict note: none. File paths, function names and line numbers in the issue match the current ref.

1. Files likely to change
- `tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py` (only file)
- No changelog fragment: CLAUDE.md §20 (around line 676) exempts test-only changes.

2. Functions or modules to implement
- `_run_security_audit`: in the `env.update({...})` block next to `"AI_ENGINE_SECURITY_AUDIT": "codex"`, add `"AI_ENGINE_LABELS": "[]"`. Add a short comment pointing to the `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` fallback in `claude_engine.work_item_labels`. Because `extra_env` is applied after this block, the second case in line 2723 (`"AI_ENGINE_LABELS": '["ai:codex"]'`) still overrides it.
- New test `test_security_audit_engine_ignores_ci_event_labels(tmp_path, monkeypatch)`:
  - Write an event JSON file with `{"pull_request": {"labels": [{"name": "ai:engine-claude"}]}}`.
  - `monkeypatch.setenv("GITHUB_EVENT_PATH", <file>)`.
  - Call `_claude_engine_audit(..., claude_env={"AI_ENGINE_SECURITY_AUDIT": "codex"})`.
  - Assert `returncode == 0`, `"security-audit: engine=codex" in proc.stdout`, `not state.get("claude_calls")`, and `_kept_ids(payload) == ["codex-finding"]`.
  - This test fails without the fix and passes with it.

3. Data structures affected
- Only the subprocess env dict in the test harness. No state, schema or label contract changes.

4. API or interface changes
- None. Tests that need real labels keep passing `AI_ENGINE_LABELS` through `extra_env` / `claude_env`.

## Decisions

### D1 — Pin `AI_ENGINE_LABELS` to `[]` instead of stripping `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`
- Chosen: default `AI_ENGINE_LABELS="[]"` in the harness env block, before `extra_env` is applied.
- Alternatives considered: add `"GITHUB_EVENT_PATH"` to the prefix filter at line ~250, as `tests/test_ai_engine.py:130` and `tests/test_claude_engine.py:39` do; or both.
- Why: `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` is also read by `scripts/load_workflow_overlay.py`, so stripping it could change unrelated behaviour in the audit subprocess. Setting `AI_ENGINE_LABELS` affects only engine selection, which is the defect. `work_item_labels` treats any present key, even `[]`, as authoritative, and `extra_env` can still override the default.

### D2 — Add a regression test that injects a hostile event payload
- Chosen: a dedicated test that sets `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` to an event with an `ai:engine-claude` label.
- Alternatives considered: rely on the fixed harness without a reproducer.
- Why: the original failure depended on the CI environment and never showed up locally. The reproducer makes the isolation contract hold on every runner.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries touched: none in production. This is a test harness change only.
- Authorization: no new endpoint or surface.
- External input validation: unchanged. The event payload is still parsed by the unchanged `work_item_labels`.
- Abuse cases: none introduced. The fix stops a PR's labels from silently changing which engine paths the contract test exercises, so the "Codex never starts Claude" guarantee is tested deterministically.

5. Risks and edge cases
- `AI_ENGINE_LABELS` may be re-derived by `scripts/security_audit.sh` or `scripts/ai_engine.sh` before it reaches Python. Comments at `security_audit.sh:1391` and `ai_engine.sh:13,51` show it is passed through as the work-item label list. If the shell used `${AI_ENGINE_LABELS:-}` with a fallback, `"[]"` is still non-empty, so it is safe either way. The implementer should confirm with the regression test.
- Other tests in this file that expect `source=default` (`test_security_audit_role_default_runs_claude`) keep working: an empty label list gives no label source.
- Local runs without `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` behave as before.

6. Testing considerations
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m pytest tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py -q` (whole module; it lives in CI job `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`).
- Run the new test once with the harness change reverted locally to confirm it reproduces the failure (`engine=claude`, or a `claude_calls` entry).
- Also run `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH=<event with ai:engine-claude> python -m pytest tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py -k "engine or claude"` to simulate CI.
- `ruff check tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py`. Keep tab indentation as in the file.

7. Pre-execution self-check
- Root cause is grounded in code read in this run: harness lines 246-272 and 2722-2729, `claude_engine.py` 330-355 and 394-414.
- The fix is a single file, test-only, and does not change any production identifier.
- No workflow file, script, label contract or changelog fragment changes. No new env var reaches production code.
- Assumption: the CI PR carried `ai:engine-claude`. The triage logs do not show the payload, but the fix makes the test independent of the payload whatever the label was.
